title: fusion.entry-result/v2
description: fusion's proposal in request 77, not yet accepted by Prior: the result of the run step of fusion.entry.v2 and the module's envelope for the invocation, bound by workflows/entry.v2.json whatever the entry's profile declares (decision 261023-1854-which-schemas-bind-an-entry-run-of-an-agent-that-is-also-a-workflow-role, option 1). It describes delivery on Prior's step-17 model (ruling 261024-0807-how-does-an-entry-run-deliver-its-result-into-the-users-repository; decision 261027-1612-which-host-service-integrates-an-entry-run-under-the-step-17-model-and-what-does-it-replace, option 1): the run's own commits fast-forward the user's branch as made, and its uncommitted changes are applied to the user's checkout and stay uncommitted there. status takes four values: completed, the run ended in success and every step after it completed; refused, the invocation, admission, an answer or a host step refused, with the reason in violations; recovery-required, a role or host effect is unknown or in flight, never a fabricated answer and never a terminal refusal written to end the run; ended, the run stopped, the user having ended the session through a question (Prior's question outcome ended) or by the stop the entry offers, which is neither a success nor an interruption that discards the workspace. ending is how the run ended in the class and reason form of Prior's fusion-surface comparison (internal/qualification/fusionsurface Ending), null only on recovery-required, which is no ending. questions are the run's host.question.v1 calls with their answers, in call order; commits and delta the integration's; all three are read from the host's receipts and copied, never composed by the model. Settlement is not acceptance: a settled run whose answer was refused stays settled, and a retry is a new invocation with a new workflow_id and run_id. No $schema keyword: the host compiles every bundle schema as draft 2020-12 and this file must carry no URL.

class.description: success, the role produced its final answer; refusal, the run or a step refused; stop, the run stopped before its final answer.

reason.description: A reason category, lowercase and hyphenated, such as stopped-by-user; never free model text.

questions.description: One entry per host.question.v1 call of the run, in call order; empty when the run asked nothing.

call_id.description: The call's slot within the run.

options.description: The call's options; empty on the chat-text channel.

selected.description: The options chosen, each among options; empty unless outcome is answered on ask-user-question.

text.description: The answer's text; empty unless outcome is answered.

commits.description: The run's own commits, fast-forwarded onto the user's branch as the run made them, oldest first, copied from the host.entry.integrate.v1 answer; empty when the run made no commit or no integration happened.

reference.description: The user's branch reference the commit was fast-forwarded onto, the one the user's HEAD named (such as refs/heads/main), the answer's reference.

subject.description: The commit's own subject line, as the run wrote it.

changes.description: One per path the commit changed, in git's name-status form as the host assembles it: "<status>\t<path>" for A, D, M and T, "<status><score>\t<old path>\t<new path>" for C and R; each path relative to the repository root.

delta.description: The run's uncommitted changes, applied to the user's checkout and left uncommitted there, in the same name-status form, copied from the host.entry.integrate.v1 answer; empty when there were none or no integration happened.

violations.description: Why the answer is not completed; empty on completed.

name_status.description: One line of git's name-status form with the tab separators: a status letter and a path, or a C or R status with its similarity score and two paths. No path is absolute or empty, and none carries a tab or a newline.
